note:
Level 1, both label levels read (.sav copied from the wallace_2026_s2c_desirecert cache; sha256 77e72d25dd6fc1f8800272508884584543e1b81e4b452795fbf26e8c40e4732e verified; the S2c .sps contains no intoluncert text). CODE DERIVATION: SINGLE spec s2c_intoluncert.csv = (s2c, [(intoluncert{i} -> intoluncert{i}, rev 0) for i in 1..5]): the code IS the source column name (.sav columns 83-87, 0-based 82-86). No '-' flip prefix, so resp is the deposited value and the live table has no itemcov_recoded column. Exempt from Step 5b (source-name derivation), no verification files. TEXT: variable labels shipped verbatim except that Qualtrics line-break artifacts ('My
mind', 'Uncertainty
makes', 'When
I', 'I
must') were replaced by single spaces; curly apostrophes (U+2019) kept as in the file. No lead-in in any label, instructions left blank. OPTIONS: all five points value-labelled identically on all items: 1 Describes me extremely well, 2 Describes me very well, 3 Describes me moderately well, 4 Describes me slightly well, 5 Does not describe me; shipped verbatim. INSTRUMENT: the five labels are verbatim IUS-27 (Freeston et al. 1994; English Buhr & Dugas 2002) items 3, 5, 6, 15, 25 as printed on PhenX protocol 650701; the study replaced the IUS anchors (1 = not at all characteristic of me ... 5 = entirely characteristic of me) with its own reversed describes-me anchors. DIRECTION: 1 = Describes me extremely well, so high resp = less intolerance of uncertainty. Corroborated: item means 3.18-3.76 (does-not-describe side, plausible for a general sample); r = +0.25 to +0.39 with desireforcert1/desireforcert (1 = Strongly agree) and -0.16 to -0.36 with selfcert1-2 (1 = very much ... 7 = not at all) -- intolerant people want certainty more and feel less certain, consistent only with the labelled direction. Inter-item r 0.60-0.75, no reverse-worded items. The script docstring's '... 7 = does not describe me' is wrong: source and live are 1..5. COUNTS: source 793 rows, 793 non-missing per item; live 3965 rows = 793 ids x 5; per-item resp-count vectors (1..5) source = live exactly: intoluncert1 35/89/178/266/225, intoluncert2 59/109/166/217/242, intoluncert3 99/156/168/247/123, intoluncert4 62/111/172/236/212, intoluncert5 50/93/136/231/283. RIGHTS: instrument_rights_register.csv row 'Intolerance of Uncertainty Scale (IUS, 27 items)' carries verdict ship_with_note (2026-09-23 Ben, irw#2381 rights bank R08); applied, not re-derived, no register row written. Its clause, from the distributor PhenX (https://www.phenxtoolkit.org/protocols/view/650701, re-fetched 2026-09-28): 'This protocol is freely available; permission not required for use.' Its caution: this is a distributor statement, not an originator grant -- Freeston 1994 / Buhr & Dugas 2002 terms were not located, and an originator page stating terms, if ever read, would govern over the register row. It does not block because nothing located reserves a right (no fee, permission, NC, ND or redistribution clause); silence is permission. English administration, so the register's English-only scope is satisfied. Wording here was copied from the study's own .sav labels, not from PhenX.
public_note: Responses run 1 = Describes me extremely well to 5 = Does not describe me, so a higher value means less intolerance of uncertainty -- the reverse of the usual Intolerance of Uncertainty Scale scoring.
